question: What is the term for the movement of tectonic plates causing earthquakes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plate tectonics**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plate tectonics** is the scientific theory that describes the large-scale motion of the seven large plates and the movements of a larger number of smaller plates of Earth's **lithosphere**.
 
• Earthquakes occur when these tectonic plates interact at their boundaries. The friction between the plates causes **stress** to build up; when this stress is suddenly released, it sends **seismic waves** through the Earth's crust, resulting in an earthquake.
 
• **Erosion** is a geological process in which earthen materials are worn away and transported by natural forces such as wind or water, which does not cause tectonic earthquakes.
 
• **Sedimentation** is the tendency for particles in suspension to settle out of the fluid in which they are entrained and come to rest against a barrier, a process unrelated to plate movement.
 
• **Convection** (specifically mantle convection) is the slow creeping motion of Earth's solid silicate mantle caused by convection currents carrying heat from the interior to the surface. While it is the **driving force** behind plate movement, the movement itself and the resulting earthquakes are categorized under the theory of **Plate tectonics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The theory of plate tectonics built upon the concept of **Continental Drift**, an idea first proposed by scientist **Alfred Wegener** in 1912.
 
• There are three primary types of plate boundaries: **Divergent** (moving apart), **Convergent** (moving together), and **Transform** (sliding past each other).
 
• Most of the world's earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur along the **Pacific Ring of Fire**, which is a direct result of plate tectonics and the movement of several major and minor tectonic plates.
 
• The point inside the Earth where the earthquake starts is called the **Hypocenter** (or focus), and the point directly above it on the surface is the **Epicenter**.
